posts.title: Fossil fuels dumped from latest draft deal
posts.text: Every mention of fossil fuels has been expunged from the draft text for the main outcome of the Cop31 UN climate summit, in a blow to the vulnerable countries which had fought hard for its inclusion. The “transition away from fossil fuels” was in the first 18-page draft, published on Monday, but missing from the…

Now that a new draft of the cover decision has been released, the whole Cop31 venue is humming with the sound of people hitting “Ctrl+F” on their keyboards to see if their issue of choice has survived, or how it has been described. So Ctrl+F “Fossil” shows that word doesn’t appear in the latest text, which may create…

Hello, it’s Ajit Niranjan here, taking back over from Matthew Pearce. Proper analysis of the new draft is coming from our colleagues on the ground, but I can tell you that a quick Ctrl+F for “fossil fuels”, the fundamental cause of the climate crisis, no longer yields any results. Let’s see what has survived …
The new draft text is out. And the first thing to notice is that it has nearly halved in length. On Monday there were 144 paragraphs; now there are just 80.

The debate over how electrification will be addressed in the final text continues is still under way, with sharp divisions remaining on whether the presidency’s 35% by 2035 pledge should require a tie-in to renewable energy. But that doesn’t mean there hasn’t been progress on electrification – a key priority set by…

Ding ding! Climate campaigners 350.org have staged a boxing-themed protest outside Cop to call for an electrification target based on renewable energy, not fossil fuels. The group say 200,000 people from around the world have signed a petition calling on the Cop31 presidencies to ensure countries commit to a real…

While countries waited for a new draft text on Thursday, which was planned for early afternoon but is now likely to be delayed, the mood remained cooperative and constructive. Several countries reported being cheered by the “divan” meeting that took place on Wednesday evening. Named for a “council” under the Ottoman…
